title: Bayesian Gaussian Copula Endogeneity Correction
text: Package website: https://ashgreat.github.io/endogCopulaBayes/ endogCopulaBayes implements Bayesian Gaussian copula endogeneity correction Haschka (2022b; published 2026 Oxford Bulletin Economics Statistics “Bayesian Inference Joint Estimation Models Using Copulas Handle Endogenous Regressors”). estimator handles endogenous regressor without instruments modelling joint distribution regressors regression error Gaussian copula sampling unknowns — regression coefficients, residual variance, copula correlations, (Dirichlet) probability masses describing marginal distributions regressors — Metropolis-within-Gibbs MCMC sampler. code faithful port published replication scripts (CopRegBAYES.R) copula-based endogeneity corrections research code; packaged sampler reproduces reference chain draw draw.

title: Bayesian Gaussian Copula Endogeneity Correction
Bayesian Gaussian Copula Endogeneity Correction
text: CopRegBayes() two interfaces: formula interface, CopRegBayes(y ~ endog | exog, data = ...): one endogenous regressor bar, one exogenous regressor (Haschka (2026) sampler supports exactly one ). data-frame interface (legacy), CopRegBayes(data), still works unchanged expects data frame exactly columns (extra columns ignored): Notes: intercept column (const) added internally — include one data. Rows missing values dropped sampling. Regressors must numeric; factors supported. model estimated y = beta_0 + beta_z * endog + beta_x * exog + e, Gaussian copula linking endog, exog, e; correlation exog e restricted zero (exogeneity exog).

title: Bayesian Gaussian Copula Endogeneity Correction
text: data-frame interface remains fully supported existing code: returned object (class endog_copula_bayes) carries full MCMC chain burned-, thinned posterior matrix. Columns 1–7 named model parameters (beta_0, beta_z, beta_x, sigma2, rho_zx, rho_ze, rho_xe), followed 2 * N unnamed Dirichlet probability masses marginals z x, three hyperprior variances (hyper_a, hyper_b1, hyper_b2). fit via formula interface, summary() print() label beta_z / beta_x rows real endogenous/exogenous variable names (price income), original names recorded fit$variables. See ?CopRegBayes details.
code: library(endogCopulaBayes)  # Simulate data with an endogenous, log-normally distributed price set.seed(1) n <- 200 sigma <- matrix(c(1, .7, 0,                   .7, 1, .3,                   0, .3, 1), nrow = 3, byrow = TRUE) eps <- mvtnorm::rmvnorm(n, sigma = sigma) price <- qlnorm(pnorm(eps[, 2]))          # endogenous (correlated with the error) income <- qnorm(pnorm(eps[, 3]))          # exogenous e <- qnorm(pnorm(eps[, 1]), sd = sqrt(2)) dat <- data.frame(sales = 2 - 4 * price + 6 * income + e,                   price = price, income = income)  # Fit (use many more iterations in real applications) fit <- CopRegBayes(sales ~ price | income, data = dat,                    iterations = 10000, burnin = 2000, thin = 10, seed = 42)  fit             # posterior means, labelled with the original variable names summary(fit)    # mean, sd, median, and 95% credible intervals dat_legacy <- data.frame(y = dat$sales, z = dat$price, x = dat$income) fit_legacy <- CopRegBayes(dat_legacy, iterations = 10000, burnin = 2000,                           thin = 10, seed = 42)

title: Bayesian Gaussian Copula Endogeneity Correction
text: endogCopula — cross-sectional copula endogeneity corrections (Park & Gupta 2012; Yang et al. 2025; Hu et al. 2025; Breitung et al. 2024; Haschka 2024; Liengaard et al. 2025). endogCopulaPanel — fixed-effects panel maximum-likelihood estimator Haschka (2022).

title: Bayesian Gaussian Copula Sampler — CopRegBayes
text: Metropolis-within-Gibbs sampler copula-based endogeneity correction Haschka. chain columns laid reference implementation: columns 1–3 hold regression coefficients (beta_0, beta_z, beta_x), column 4 residual variance (sigma2), columns 5–7 copula correlations (rho_zx endogenous exogenous regressor, rho_ze endogenous regressor error, rho_xe exogenous regressor error, latter forced zero), columns 8:(N + 7) Dirichlet probability masses distribution z, columns (N + 8):(2 * N + 7) Dirichlet probability masses distribution x, final three columns hyperprior variances normal priors regression coefficients (hyper_a, hyper_b1, hyper_b2). Dirichlet mass columns left unnamed.

title: Bayesian Gaussian Copula Sampler — CopRegBayes
text: object class endog_copula_bayes: list components chain Numeric matrix dimension (iterations + 1) x (2 * N + 10) holding full MCMC chain, one draw per row. columns follow layout described : seven named model parameters, 2 * N unnamed Dirichlet probability masses (N z, N x), three hyperprior variances. posterior Numeric matrix columns chain, discarding first burnin rows keeping every thin-th remaining row. parameters Character vector names ten tracked (named) parameters summarised summary.endog_copula_bayes(). n Number complete observations used. iterations, burnin, thin, seed sampler settings supplied. variables NULL data-frame interface; formula interface, list original response, endogenous, exogenous variable names.

Use formula interface (y ~ endog | exog) legacy data-frame interface (data frame columns y, z, x); dispatch underlying sampler seeded fit identical either way. formula interface additionally records original variable names ($variables) uses label beta_z / beta_x rows print.endog_copula_bayes() summary.endog_copula_bayes().

code: set.seed(1) n <- 60 z <- rlnorm(n) x <- rnorm(n) dat <- data.frame(y = 2 - 4 * z + 6 * x + rnorm(n, sd = sqrt(2)),                   z = z, x = x) fit <- CopRegBayes(dat, iterations = 100, burnin = 20, thin = 2, seed = 42) fit #> Bayesian Gaussian copula regression (Haschka) #> Observations: 60 #> Iterations: 100 (burn-in 20, thinning 2, 41 posterior draws) #>  #> Posterior means: #>    beta_0    beta_z    beta_x    sigma2    rho_zx    rho_ze    rho_xe   hyper_a  #>    2.1708   -4.1770    5.6646    2.2923   -0.0621    0.1038    0.0000  230.4490  #>  hyper_b1  hyper_b2  #> 1744.2163  547.1008  summary(fit) #> Bayesian Gaussian copula regression (Haschka) #> Observations: 60 #> Iterations: 100 (burn-in 20, thinning 2, 41 posterior draws) #>  #> Posterior summary: #>               mean        sd  median    2.5%     97.5% #> beta_0      2.1708    0.4746  1.9885  1.7091    3.0271 #> beta_z     -4.1770    0.2729 -4.0512 -4.6916   -3.8495 #> beta_x      5.6646    0.1503  5.6206  5.4646    5.9248 #> sigma2      2.2923    0.3857  2.1896  1.5984    3.0272 #> rho_zx     -0.0621    0.1324 -0.0587 -0.2963    0.1994 #> rho_ze      0.1038    0.2357  0.0090 -0.2172    0.5247 #> rho_xe      0.0000    0.0000  0.0000  0.0000    0.0000 #> hyper_a   230.4490  586.0057  8.4011  0.8192 2364.4946 #> hyper_b1 1744.2163 9555.6623 56.5276  4.2783 4077.6518 #> hyper_b2  547.1008 1882.5218 79.5511 11.3015 1344.0010  # \donttest{ # Equivalent formula interface (variable names are used as labels) fit_f <- CopRegBayes(y ~ z | x, data = dat, iterations = 100, burnin = 20,                      thin = 2, seed = 42) summary(fit_f) #> Bayesian Gaussian copula regression (Haschka) #> Observations: 60 #> Iterations: 100 (burn-in 20, thinning 2, 41 posterior draws) #>  #> Posterior summary: #>               mean        sd  median    2.5%     97.5% #> beta_0      2.1708    0.4746  1.9885  1.7091    3.0271 #> z          -4.1770    0.2729 -4.0512 -4.6916   -3.8495 #> x           5.6646    0.1503  5.6206  5.4646    5.9248 #> sigma2      2.2923    0.3857  2.1896  1.5984    3.0272 #> rho_zx     -0.0621    0.1324 -0.0587 -0.2963    0.1994 #> rho_ze      0.1038    0.2357  0.0090 -0.2172    0.5247 #> rho_xe      0.0000    0.0000  0.0000  0.0000    0.0000 #> hyper_a   230.4490  586.0057  8.4011  0.8192 2364.4946 #> hyper_b1 1744.2163 9555.6623 56.5276  4.2783 4077.6518 #> hyper_b2  547.1008 1882.5218 79.5511 11.3015 1344.0010 # text: Computes effective sample size (ESS) Geweke (1992) convergence z-score named model parameters (regression coefficients, residual variance, copula correlations, hyperprior variances) using thinned posterior sample stored object$posterior. 2 * N unnamed Dirichlet probability masses included.
